title: Dynamic dequant rewrite for sliced prefill with late-binding mixed-precision kernels
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: For long-context workloads we slice prefill requests into fixed chunks to keep latency and memory predictable. When serving mixed-precision models (INT8 fast path and FP8 fallback) the current runtime performs dequantization eagerly on each slice which creates repeated CPU/GPU memory traffic and stalls decode. This is visible as a 12-25% token throughput regression on sliced prefill profiles compared to contiguous prefill.

Goal: Implement a dynamic dequant rewrite pass that: (1) identifies slice-aligned KV lifecycles, (2) emits a late-binding dequant operator that can be fused into the decode kernel when possible, and (3) exposes a kernel selector hint so the scheduler can choose an INT8 or FP8 fused path at the last moment based on available capacity and run-time precision budget.

Approach:
- Add a Pass in the prefill planner that tags KV buffers with slice-id and a \"dequant_mode\" hint (eager|late-bind|none).
- Implement a lightweight GPU-side late-dequant operator that stores a compact quant-epilogue descriptor and defers per-token dequant until decode is scheduled.
- Extend kernel selection to consider \"late-bind\" compatibility and prefer fused decode+dequant kernels when sequence length and batch shapes match optimized shapes.
- Provide a fallback to eager dequant for workloads where fused path increases peak memory beyond configured SLO.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end perf for sliced prefill workloads shows >=10% throughput improvement and <=5ms median latency increase compared to current baseline.
- No regressions on contiguous prefill or small-batch low-latency profiles.
- Feature gated by runtime flag and covered by unit tests and integration benchmarks.
- Telemetry: emit dequant_mode and selected_kernel in trace spans and console dashboards.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Late-binding increases scheduler complexity and may complicate autoscaling heuristics; mitigation: keep the feature off by default and enable only for configured queues.
- Fusion successful only for a subset of shapes; we will maintain detailed perf matrix and automated rollout by percentage.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement pass + GPU late-dequant operator behind feature flag.
2) Add kernel selector hint and unit tests.
3) Internal canary across 5% of traffic on dedicated cluster with long-context workloads.
4) Monitor token throughput, GPU memory, and decode latency; iterate.

2025-02-25 - Mateo: Implemented Pass and added kernel selector hint. CI failing on one unit test due to alignment assumptions in the allocator; working on fix in PR #4139.
2025-02-27 - Anika (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Add telemetry for dequant_mode and selected_kernel, and ensure we can toggle per-queue via console before canary.
2025-03-01 - Code review: PR 4127 approved with comments to document fallback memory cost. Linked a follow-up ticket for allocator changes if we decide to keep late-bind on by default (ENG-91402).

2025-03-04 - Perf: Internal canary run (10% on dedicated-longctx) shows token throughput +12% and median decode latency +3.2ms. GPU memory increased by 1.8% peak on INT8 fused path. Proceed to wider canary pending ops sign-off.
